cases.title: approve() has no per-signer tracking, letting a single signer reach the threshold alone
cases.status: confirmed by an executable Foundry PoC (test/TimeLockedMultisigExploit.t.sol, passing)
cases.description: TimeLockedMultisig.approve() increments a raw counter (`p.approvals`) on every call from any signer, with NO record of which specific signer already approved a given proposal. A single signer can therefore call approve() repeatedly on the same proposal id and single-handedly drive `p.approvals` up to `threshold`, at which point the timelock clock (`p.readyAt`) starts — completely defeating the purpose of an N-of-M multisig, since zero OTHER signers' consent was ever required or obtained. This is not a reentrancy or access-control-bypass bug in the usual sense (the caller IS a legitimate signer, `onlySigner` correctly gates the call) — it's a missing-deduplication bug: the contract's own state model has no way to distinguish '3 different signers each approved once' from 'one signer approved 3 times'.
cases.source_richness: high — the bug lives in this repo's own 71-line contract, executable PoC included (test/TimeLockedMultisigExploit.t.sol), exact scenario: a 2-of-3 multisig where signerA alone calls approve() twice, reaching the threshold with zero participation from signerB or signerC, then successfully executes a 5 ETH transfer after the timelock elapses.
